chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from Nasih the Mu'adhdhin, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I pray in the house and then go out to them [the congregation].' He said, 'Make it a voluntary prayer and do not say Takbir with them, so that you enter with them in the prayer, for indeed the key to the prayer is the Takbir.'

key_terms.اَلتَّكْبِيرُ: The saying of 'Allahu Akbar', the opening declaration of prayer

ai.seo_question: How should one join a congregational prayer if they have already prayed individually at home?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia jurisprudential principle of *ittiba'* (following) in congregational prayer, emphasizing the importance of synchronizing the follower's status with the Imam. By designating the initial home prayer as *nafl* and withholding the opening *Takbir al-Ihram*, the worshipper avoids creating a separate prayer entity, thereby ensuring his entry into the congregation is seamless and valid. This practice highlights the Shia emphasis on the structural integrity of the prayer unit (*rak'ah*) and the precise moment of joining the Imam.
